text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness. To begin our evaluation, how many days postpartum are you, and has your fever been constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis (uterine infection).

The patient is 24 years old, 11 days postpartum (inferred from "11 pound boy" typo as 11 days, or simply focusing on the symptoms), presenting with fever, abdominal (uterine) tenderness, and increased urinary frequency. The history of prolonged labor is a significant risk factor for this condition. The decrease in bowel sounds and uterine tenderness suggest possible pelvic inflammation or abscess formation.

To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I would like to request a CBC with differential, C-reactive protein (CRP), and a pelvic ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Pelvic_Ultrasound
